📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

⭐️ Adam Back criticizes BIP-110 supporters after failed Bitcoin fork 

🌐 Blockstream CEO Adam Back has renewed his criticism of Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 110 (BIP-110), arguing that attempts to impose controversial network changes have repeatedly failed to gain market support. In a November 3 post on X, Back referenced earlier commentary from Bitcoin advocate Francis Pouliot while addressing supporters of the proposed Bitcoin fork.

📌 “Attempts to impose your views on bitcoin get market rejected,” Back wrote, pointing to previous disputes over Bitcoin’s rules. He described Pouliot’s commentary as a “masterclass on bitcoin reality” and said discussions about Bitcoin’s established rules were intended to help people understand immutability. Back’s latest comments followed renewed discussion about BIP-110, a proposal designed to restrict certain forms of non-financial data on Bitcoin.

➡️ He argued that the market would resist efforts to override consensus, even when supporters believed their proposed changes were beneficial.Back further claimed that BIP-110 “failed the first gate hard” because of what he described as serious technical problems. The criticism continued a position he adopted earlier this year, when he warned that the proposal could divide Bitcoin’s network.

The Healing Power of Elvis’s 
“An American Trilogy” 🇺🇸🎤

When Elvis Presley took the stage in 1972 and 1973, he wasn't just entertaining, he was orchestrating a powerful moment of national healing.

His legendary performance of "An American Trilogy" (famously captured during the groundbreaking 1973 Aloha from Hawaii satellite broadcast) remains one of the most culturally significant moments in music history. 

But what was he actually trying to say?

While the medley was originally arranged by Mickey Newbury as a melancholy folk lament during the Vietnam War, Elvis reimagined it as a grand, soaring statement of unity for a fractured nation.

By weaving together three vastly different 19th-century songs, Elvis confronted the complex fabric of the American identity head-on:

• "Dixie" – The unofficial Confederate anthem, rendered not as a battle cry, but as a slow, mournful look at the old South.

• "All My Trials" – A powerful African American spiritual carrying the profound sorrow and resilience of enslaved people.

• "The Battle Hymn of the Republic" – The triumphant marching anthem of the Union Army.

Instead of avoiding the deep-seated pain of the Civil War or the civil rights struggles of the 1970s, Elvis used his platform to smash these opposing traditions together. Backed by the powerhouse gospel vocals of The Sweet Inspirations, he abstracted America's heavy history into raw, spiritual emotion. 

He moved the audience from an intimate, gentle lullaby to a booming orchestral crescendo proving that out of deep division, hope and reconciliation are possible.

Elvis was so deeply invested in this message that he even set aside other major commercial releases just to get this medley to the world. 

It wasn't just a live showstopper; it was Elvis’s definitive statement on the complex, beautiful, and enduring American dream. 🇺🇸

GOP in Free Fall: 2028 Presidential Hopefuls See Their Chance to Seize Power


The Republican Party is reeling from a devastating midterm defeat, and the scramble to control its future has already begun. 

With Democrats taking command of both chambers of Congress, potential Republican presidential contenders are wasting little time positioning themselves as the leaders who can rescue a party in crisis. Behind the scenes, the political blame game is intensifying.

Few Republicans are willing to openly challenge Trump, but several are making it clear that the GOP needs a serious course correction. And as JD Vance’s once-promising path to the 2028 nomination suddenly looks less certain, ambitious rivals are beginning to see an opening.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis was among the first to seize the moment. Calling the Republican collapse an «extinction-level event,» he portrayed Florida as a rare GOP stronghold and pointed to his own record as proof that he knows how to win when the party is struggling.

Former Vice President Pence delivered an even sharper indictment, attacking the administration’s spending, mounting national debt, tariffs and handling of Iran. He argued that voters had turned against the party’s drift toward economic populism and warned Republicans they had lost touch with their conservative principles.

Rep. Elise Stefanik called the results a political reckoning and an opportunity for a reset, while stopping short of breaking with Trump. Former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo also urged Republicans to rethink their priorities, arguing that neither the left nor big-government conservatives were offering Americans the opportunity they wanted.

However, the most consequential criticism may be coming from within Trump’s own administration. Vance openly blamed the Iran war for the Republican defeat, arguing that any honest discussion about the party’s future must begin with the conflict. 

Texas Sen. Ted Cruz echoed that assessment, pointing to tariffs and a growing disconnect between Republicans and ordinary Americans. 

He called for a return to free-market conservatism. Meanwhile, former New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie took direct aim at Vance, warning that his political legacy could be damaged by defending controversial Republican allies.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, another potential 2028 contender, has remained publicly silent. The stakes could hardly be higher. Trump’s influence still looms over the GOP, but the midterm disaster has cracked open a battle for succession. 

Every Republican hopeful is now trying to answer the same question: who can rebuild the party — and who will be blamed for its collapse?

👀 Justin Sun becomes PEPE’s largest individual holder, Arkham says 

🌐 Tron founder Justin Sun has accumulated nearly 3% of PEPE’s supply, with blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identifying approximately $51.25 million worth of the memecoin across his known and suspected wallets. According to an October 27 Arkham Intelligence report, the tokens entered Sun-linked wallets over the previous 10 days, making him the largest individual PEPE holder outside cryptocurrency exchanges.

🔗 The firm estimated his combined holdings at 2.82% of PEPE’s supply, although some wallets included in its calculations were attributed to Sun through blockchain analysis. At the time, PEPE had a market capitalization of approximately $1.81 billion, with exchanges controlling several of the largest known holdings.

📊 Binance held $337.5 million worth of PEPE, representing 18.7% of the supply, followed by Robinhood with $150.9 million, or 8.37%. Coinbase and OKX accounted for another 5.03% and 4.15%, respectively. Unlike Sun’s attributed holdings, exchange balances generally include assets held on behalf of customers, meaning their large positions do not necessarily represent investments made by the platforms themselves.
